task_dynamic_1781410213_0.goal: Formalize and model the Collatz function and conjecture axioms.

steps.name: Literature Review and Mathematical Definition
steps.description: Conduct a detailed review of the Collatz conjecture. Formally define the function $C(n)$ and gather existing axiomatic frameworks or common conjectures associated with its behavior (e.g., termination, cycle structure). Initial drafting should establish a strong mathematical foundation.

steps.name: Functional Implementation and Unit Testing
steps.description: Implement the Collatz function $C(n)$ in a verifiable programming language (e.g., Python). Write unit tests to verify the core arithmetic operations and behavior for various input values ($n=1$, even $n$, odd $n$). Focus on creating a robust, executable model of the conjecture.

steps.name: Modeling and Conjecture Formalization Output
steps.description: Compile the mathematical findings (Step 1) and the executable model results (Step 2). Create a comprehensive report that formally presents the conjecture axioms, discusses the modeled function's behavior for tested values, and summarizes the current state of formal proof challenges. This output must be ready for presentation.

task_dynamic_1781410213_1.goal: Develop advanced computational verification algorithms (e.g., massive data testing, pattern recognition) to find counterexamples or prove convergence for defined ranges.

steps.name: Literature Review and Algorithm Design
steps.description: Research advanced computational verification techniques (e.g., constraint solving, formal methods, specialized testing methodologies like fuzzing or model checking). Select 2-3 promising algorithms/approaches suitable for finding counterexamples or proving convergence within defined ranges. Outline the structure for input definition, hypothesis formulation, and output verification.

steps.name: Implementation of Core Verification Engine
steps.description: Develop the foundational code structure for the chosen algorithms. This involves writing modules to handle input generation (massive data testing setup), implementing pattern recognition logic (e.g., statistical analysis or symbolic execution framework), and integrating the core verification loop that tests hypotheses against defined ranges.

steps.name: Testing and Benchmarking
steps.description: Implement comprehensive test cases using established benchmarks and generated synthetic data to rigorously validate the verification engine. Test scenarios must cover edge cases, expected convergence paths, and suspected failure points to demonstrate robustness before final documentation.

steps.name: Final Analysis and Reporting
steps.description: Execute the fully integrated verification system using challenging datasets defined by the task scope. Systematically document any discovered counterexamples or mathematically prove convergence for the defined ranges. Summarize the findings, limitations, and recommendations in a comprehensive report.

task_dynamic_1781410213_2.goal: Synthesize evidence from formal logic, number theory, and computation to construct a definitive proof or disprove the conjecture.

steps.name: Literature Review and Conjecture Formulation
steps.description: The research agents must independently review existing literature in formal logic (e.g., proof theory, model theory), number theory (specific branches relevant to the conjecture, e.g., elliptic curves, p-adic analysis), and computation (computability theory, complexity classes). This step concludes with the formalization of the conjecture into a precise mathematical statement ($ orall x, P(x) ightarrow Q(x)$) and identifying known related open problems or necessary premises.

steps.name: Independent Proof Strategy Development and Simulation
steps.description: Multiple specialized agents (e.g., a Logic Agent, a Number Theory Agent, and a Computational Agent) will operate in parallel. Each agent develops an initial proof strategy based on their domain expertise and attempts to find counterexamples or necessary conditions that constrain the conjecture. They must write out structured proofs/disproof arguments using LaTeX snippets and identify gaps or required computational checks.

steps.name: Integration and Hypothesis Testing
steps.description: The findings from all specialized agents must be synthesized. A dedicated Synthesis Agent reviews the arguments, ensuring internal consistency between the formal logic constraints (A), number theoretic invariants (B), and computational limits (C). If inconsistencies or potential proofs exist, new intermediate lemmas must be derived and tested against each other. This involves complex cross-disciplinary validation.

steps.name: Final Definitive Proof Construction and Conclusion
steps.description: All agents contribute their final, validated segments of the argument into a single master document. The goal is to provide either a complete, rigorous proof (or counterexample) or an identification of necessary unproven axioms/conditions required for resolution. The conclusion must be definitive and mathematically formalized.
